newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..f811d767543 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md @@ -0,0 +1,87 @@ +--- +title: Protect against telephony fraud with your own telecom provider +description: Configure provider fraud protections, destination and spending controls, secure your CYOT integration, monitor unusual activity, and respond to suspected fraud. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted + +# Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to prevent telephony fraud and configure appropriate protections for my CYOT integration. +--- + +# Protect against telephony fraud with your own telecom provider + + + + +With Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT), SMS and voice traffic runs through your own telecom provider account. You control the fraud protections, allowed destinations, and spending limits that match your organization's traffic and risk profile. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Set up your provider's fraud and spending controls before you move production traffic to CYOT. + + + +## Shared responsibility + +| Owner | Responsibility | +|---|---| +| Microsoft | Protects code generation and validation in Microsoft Entra ID, and the handoff to your endpoint. | +| Your organization | Manages the provider account, secures the integration, and configures fraud controls. | +| Telecom provider | Delivers SMS and voice, and offers fraud, destination, and spending controls. | + + + + + +## Configure fraud protections with your provider + +Work with your provider to turn on the controls available for your account: + +- **Fraud protection:** Turn on the provider's detection for suspicious SMS and voice traffic. +- **Destination restrictions:** Allow only the countries and regions where your users are. +- **Channel restrictions:** Turn on only the channels you use. +- **Spending controls:** Set usage limits and budget alerts. +- **Notifications:** Turn on alerts for unusual activity. + +> [!NOTE] +> Controls and defaults vary by provider. Ask your provider which protections are on by default and which you need to configure. + + + +## Keep your integration secure + +The setup script configures authentication and request validation for your Azure Function. Keep these settings in place, including when you customize the Function. + +Your organization is responsible for renewing and rotating the integration's application credentials and certificates. + +## Monitor for unusual activity + +Review SMS and voice volume in your provider's usage reports. A sudden increase in volume, or traffic to destinations you don't expect, can signal fraud. + + + + +## Respond to suspected fraud + +1. Contact your telecom provider to review the affected traffic. +1. Restrict the affected destinations, channels, or usage with your provider's controls. +1. Investigate the requests using the Microsoft Entra audit logs, the Function App logs, and your provider's records. +1. Update your protections before you restore traffic. + + + +## Get support + +| Issue | Contact | +|---|---| +| Fraud, provider account restrictions, delivery, or charges | Your telecom provider. Find contact details in the provider's [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/) listing. | +| Microsoft Entra authentication, code validation, or the handoff to your endpoint | Microsoft Support. See [Find help and get support for Microsoft Entra](/entra/fundamentals/how-to-get-support). | + + + +## Related content + +- [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md). +- [Monitor and troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). +- [Plan for resiliency and high availability](choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md). +- [Estimate telecom provider and Azure hosting costs](phone-providers-faq.yml#how-much-does-choose-your-own-telephony-provider-cost). +- [Security Store](/security/store/what-is-security-store).

englishSummary.headline: New guidance for protecting CYOT against telephony fraud
englishSummary.summary: A new article explains how to configure telecom-provider fraud, destination, channel, spending, and alert controls; secure the CYOT integration; monitor activity; and respond to suspected fraud.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Configure the provider’s protections before sending production traffic through CYOT, and maintain credential rotation and usage monitoring.

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..5f22e0de234 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md @@ -0,0 +1,110 @@ +--- +title: Plan for resiliency and high availability +description: Plan CYOT resiliency with multi-region Azure Functions, Azure Front Door, a secondary telecom provider, and failover and recovery testing. +ms.topic: concept-article +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted + +# Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to plan and test regional and telecom provider resiliency for my CYOT integration. +--- + +# Plan for resiliency and high availability + + + + +SMS and voice authentication sit on the critical path to your applications. When users rely on a phone code for multifactor authentication (MFA) or self-service password reset (SSPR), the availability of that code determines whether they can sign in. + +With Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT), the delivery path includes components your organization owns: the Azure Function in your subscription and your telecom provider. Design these components for resiliency so authentication stays available through regional outages and provider incidents. + + + +## Understand your delivery path + +| Component | Managed by | What it does | +|---|---|---| +| Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft | Generates and validates the code, and sends the request to your endpoint. | +| Endpoint and Azure Function | Your organization | Receives the request in your Azure subscription and sends it to your provider. | +| Telecom provider | Your provider | Delivers the SMS message or voice call to the user's phone. | + +The guided setup creates one Azure Function in a single region, connected to one telecom provider. This setup works well for evaluation and many production workloads. To protect against a regional outage or a provider incident, extend it with the options in this article. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Your organization manages the availability and recovery of the Azure resources and provider integration in your subscription. Test your resiliency design before you rely on it for production authentication. + +> [!NOTE] +> The multi-region and secondary-provider designs in this article are sample-only guidance. They aren't part of the standard deployment. Your organization is responsible for validating and maintaining these customizations. + + + +## Choose a resiliency approach + +Start with your requirements: which disruptions you must withstand, how quickly authentication must recover, and the sign-in availability your organization requires. Then choose the approach that meets them. + +| Approach | Protects against | When to use it | +|---|---|---| +| Single region, one provider (default setup) | Function App instance failures within the region | Evaluation, and production workloads that can tolerate a regional outage | +| Multi-region with Azure Front Door | Regional outages | Production workloads that require authentication during a regional disruption | +| Secondary telecom provider | Provider-specific incidents | When your primary provider alone doesn't meet your availability or coverage requirements | +| Multi-region and secondary provider | Regional outages and provider incidents | Organizations with the highest availability requirements | + + + +## Deploy across multiple regions + +A multi-region deployment uses Azure Front Door to expose one endpoint backed by Function Apps in two or more regions. Microsoft Entra ID calls the Front Door endpoint, and Front Door routes each request to a healthy region. Set it up manually after you validate a single-region deployment, because the setup script in [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md) deploys one region at a time. + +When you plan a multi-region deployment: + +- **Size each region for the full workload.** If one region is unavailable, the remaining regions must handle all authentication traffic. +- Use the same code, settings, and encryption key in every region, and coordinate certificate renewal across regions. +- **Expect failover to take time.** Some requests can fail while Front Door detects an unhealthy region and shifts traffic. +- **Plan for added cost.** Each region adds its own Function App plan, storage, Key Vault, and monitoring, plus Front Door. For estimates, see [Estimate telecom-provider and Azure hosting costs](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/COST-CALCULATOR.md). +- Adding regions improves availability, not delivery speed. SMS and voice delivery time depends mostly on your provider and carriers. + +For architecture, region and capacity planning, and step-by-step setup, see [Azure Front Door multi-region deployment](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/FRONTDOOR.md). + + + + + +## Add a secondary telecom provider + +A multi-region deployment still relies on your telecom provider. Confirm that your provider's availability commitments, redundancy, and disaster recovery meet your requirements in the countries/regions you serve. + +If one provider isn't enough, you can implement fallback to a secondary provider in your Azure Function. To avoid sending a user two codes, use the secondary provider only when the primary provider confirms it didn't accept the request. Don't resend after a timeout or unknown result, because the primary provider might already have sent the code. + +For the fallback design, see [Secondary-provider design](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/MULTI-PROVIDER-IMPLEMENTATION.md). + + + + + +## Test failover and recovery + +Before production use, test your design in a nonproduction environment: + +- Take one region or provider offline, and confirm that traffic moves to the healthy one and that it handles the full workload. +- Confirm that timeouts and unknown provider results don't trigger a second send. +- Restore the failed component, and confirm that traffic returns without errors or duplicate messages. +- Confirm that users complete SMS and voice authentication after each failover and recovery, and measure recovery time against your targets. + +Evaluation mode doesn't call your provider. Repeat your tests after any change to code, routing, configuration, or your provider integration. + +To monitor each region and provider, see [Monitor and troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). + +## Related content + +- [CYOT sample documentation](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/tree/main/docs). +- [Azure Front Door multi-region deployment](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/FRONTDOOR.md). +- [Secondary-provider design](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/docs/MULTI-PROVIDER-IMPLEMENTATION.md). +- [Reliability in Azure Functions](/azure/reliability/reliability-functions). +- [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md). +- [Prevent telephony fraud when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md). +- [Monitor and troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). +- [CYOT sample documentation (epp-packages-193-1)](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/tree/epp-packages-193-1/docs). +- [Optional multi-region onboarding with Azure Front Door (epp-packages-193-1)][sample-regions]. +- [Multi-provider implementation (epp-packages-193-1)][sample-fallback]. + +[sample-regions]: https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/epp-packages-193-1/docs/FRONTDOOR.md +[sample-fallback]: https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/epp-packages-193-1/docs/MULTI-PROVIDER-IMPLEMENTATION.md

englishSummary.headline: New CYOT resiliency and high-availability guidance
englishSummary.summary: The documentation explains CYOT delivery dependencies and resiliency approaches, including multi-region Azure Front Door deployments, secondary telecom providers, failover testing, capacity planning, and associated costs.

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md b/docs/identity/authentication/how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..3229be91ade --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md @@ -0,0 +1,277 @@ +--- +title: Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom providers +description: Deploy your telecom integration, validate evaluation mode, and gradually roll out SMS and voice delivery by using CYOT APIs. +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted + +# Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to deploy a telecom integration and configure SMS and voice delivery through Microsoft Graph. +--- + +# Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom providers + +Use Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) to deliver SMS and voice authentication through your organization's telephony provider. With CYOT, you purchase a supported provider offer through [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/), deploy the integration in your Azure subscription, and configure Microsoft Entra to route SMS or voice authentication through your provider. + +This article walks you through the end-to-end setup, including purchasing your provider offer, deploying the integration, configuring the authentication method policy, and testing the experience before moving to production. + +## How the integration works + +CYOT uses an Azure Function in your Azure subscription to connect Microsoft Entra with your telephony provider. The Azure Function processes SMS or voice requests from Microsoft Entra and sends them to your provider for delivery. + +:::image type="content" source="media/concept-phone-providers/telephony-provider-integration-diagram.jpeg" alt-text="Diagram of the CYOT integration connecting Microsoft Entra to a telephony provider through an Azure Function in your Azure subscription."::: + +## Prerequisites + +Before you begin, prepare: + +- A Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. +- An Azure subscription with a valid payment method to host the integration and subscribe to your provider. See [Security Store purchasing prerequisites](/security/store/customers/how-to-purchase-a-saas-solution-and-deploy-a-linked-solution#prerequisites). +- [Azure Cloud Shell](/azure/cloud-shell/overview) in PowerShell mode (recommended), or PowerShell 7.0+ with Azure CLI 2.61+ for integration deployment. +- A test user with a phone number registered for SMS or voice authentication. + +## Required permissions + +Use accounts with the following permissions: + +| Task | Required access | Why it's needed | +|---|---|---| +| Create the application | Permission to register applications in the customer tenant | Lets setup create the application that securely connects Microsoft Entra to your integration. | +| Deploy Azure resources | Subscription Owner, or Contributor + Role Based Access Control Administrator at the required scope | Lets setup deploy the integration in your subscription. | +| Grant directory access during deployment | Privileged Role Administrator | Lets setup grant the directory permissions that Microsoft Entra needs to route requests to your integration. | +| Read authentication method policy | Delegated `Policy.Read.AuthenticationMethod` permission and a supported role, such as Authentication Policy Administrator | Allows setup to read the existing SMS or voice authentication method configuration. | +| Update authentication method policy | Authentication Policy Administrator and delegated `Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod` permission | Allows setup to configure the SMS or voice authentication method to use the integration. | + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Before you begin, confirm that your Microsoft Entra policies allow the setup script to create the application and credentials it needs. If you use app management policies for credentials, multitenant apps, or custom Application ID URIs, review them with your Microsoft Entra administrator. + +## Step 1: Purchase and activate your telecom provider + +1. Purchase your provider's offer from [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/). For detailed purchasing instructions, see [Purchase and deploy a SaaS solution from Security Store](/security/store/customers/how-to-purchase-a-saas-solution-and-deploy-a-linked-solution). +1. After you **Place Order**, select **Configure Account Now** and follow your provider's registration instructions. +1. Keep this page available and continue to step 2. You'll complete registration in step 3 with the application ID from the deployment summary. + +## Step 2: Deploy the integration + +Use Azure Cloud Shell in PowerShell mode to run the setup script for the telecom provider you select. + +### What the setup script does + +The setup script deploys everything needed to connect Microsoft Entra ID to your telecom provider, so you don't have to create Azure resources by hand. It walks you through a few choices, then shows the full deployment plan. Nothing is created until you approve it. + +After you approve, the script creates the Microsoft Entra application, deploys and secures the Azure resources, and applies your provider's configuration. Deployment usually takes a few minutes. + +You configure the authentication method policy in step 4. + +Your organization is responsible for renewing and rotating the integration's application credentials and certificates. + +### Costs + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The integration runs on Azure resources in your subscription, billed based on your configuration and usage. To plan your budget, see [Estimate telecom-provider and Azure hosting costs](phone-providers-faq.yml#how-much-does-choose-your-own-telephony-provider-cost) before you deploy. + +### Run the setup script + +1. Sign in to the Azure portal and select the **Cloud Shell** icon (**>_**) in the top toolbar. You can also go directly to . +1. Select **PowerShell**. If Cloud Shell opens in Bash, select **Switch to PowerShell** in the toolbar. +1. If this is your first time, select **No storage account required**, choose your subscription, and then select **Apply**. +1. Download and review the [setup script](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/main/setup/Setup-Epp.ps1): + + ```powershell + Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/main/setup/Setup-Epp.ps1' ` + -OutFile '.\Setup-Epp.ps1' + ``` + +1. Run the script. + + ```powershell + .\Setup-Epp.ps1 + ``` + +1. Follow the prompts to select the customer tenant, hosting subscription, Azure region, telecom provider, runtime, and hosting plan, then approve the deployment plan. +1. Save the deployment summary, including its tenant ID, endpoint URL, and **Application (client) ID**. You need these values to complete provider registration and configure your profile. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Copy these values before you leave the Cloud Shell window. Cloud Shell sessions are temporary and can end when you navigate away, and the output isn't saved. + +## Step 3: Complete telecom provider registration + +After deployment completes, return to your telecom provider's registration page to complete the provider setup. + +1. Provide the **Application (client) ID** from your Microsoft Entra application when requested by your telecom provider. +1. Complete any additional registration steps required by the provider. +1. In [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/), go to **Management** > **My Solutions** and confirm that the **Subscription status** is '**Subscribed**' before continuing. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> Complete the telecom provider registration before configuring Microsoft Entra to send authentication traffic through the provider. + +## Step 4: Update the authentication method policy + +Configure each channel with the endpoint URL and application client ID from the deployment summary. Start in evaluation mode, validate the integration, and then gradually move delivery to your telecom provider. + +> [!WARNING] +> CYOT uses the existing SMS or voice authentication method policy. Changes to the policy, including changes to `includeTargets`, also affect the existing SMS or voice configuration. +> +> Before making updates, save the current SMS and voice settings by copying the full JSON responses from [Read the current policy](#read-the-current-policy). +> +> In a production tenant, preserve the existing `includeTargets` configuration when adding CYOT settings. Changing or removing existing targets can affect users who rely on SMS or voice authentication. +> +> Test targeting changes in a test tenant. In production, preserve the existing SMS or voice `includeTargets` and use evaluation mode plus `migrationPercentage` to validate and gradually roll out CYOT. + +### Read the current policy + +Use [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) to read and update the policy. Confirm that you're signed in to the tenant whose ID matches the Tenant ID in the deployment summary. + +Use these request URLs for the corresponding channel: + +| Channel | Request URL | +|---|---| +| SMS | `https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/Sms` | +| Voice | `https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/Voice` | + +1. Set the request method to **GET** and enter the corresponding channel's request URL. +1. Open **Modify permissions** and consent to `Policy.Read.AuthenticationMethod`. +1. Select **Run query** and save the complete JSON response as a record of the existing policy. +1. Repeat for the other channel if you're configuring both SMS and voice. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> When you prepare the updated policy, use the saved response to preserve your existing `includeTargets` and other intended authentication method settings. + +### Configure CYOT settings + +Configure these properties: + +| Property | Value | +|---|---| +| `telecomProviderSettings.url` | Endpoint URL from the deployment summary. | +| `telecomProviderSettings.appId` | Integration application client ID. | +| `telecomProviderSettings.isEvaluationModeEnabled` | Set to `true` for evaluation mode or `false` to enable telecom provider delivery. | +| `telecomProviderSettings.migrationPercentage` | Percentage of eligible authentication requests sampled during evaluation, or routed to your telecom provider when evaluation mode is disabled. | +| `includeTargets` | Preserve the existing production configuration. These targets are shared with the existing SMS or voice authentication method policy. | + +### Start in evaluation mode + +Start in evaluation mode to validate the integration before moving authentication delivery to your telecom provider. + +Use `migrationPercentage` to set the evaluation sampling percentage. + +1. Use the tested SMS or voice JSON example provided below in **Request body**. +1. Replace the endpoint URL and application client ID with the values for your deployment. +1. Set `isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `true`. +1. For production tenants, preserve the existing `includeTargets` from your saved policy configuration. Do not replace existing production targeting for CYOT testing. +1. Open **Modify permissions**, consent to `Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod`, and send the **PATCH** request to the corresponding channel's URL. +1. Read the policy again with **GET** and verify the endpoint URL, application client ID, evaluation-mode setting, migration percentage, and existing targets. +1. Complete the [evaluation-mode tests](#test-evaluation-mode) in step 5. + +> [!NOTE] +> To evaluate CYOT with a specific test user or group, perform the test in a test tenant and configure the appropriate `includeTargets` there. + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The JSON examples below contain the tested configuration values. Before using an example, replace the endpoint URL and application client ID with the values for your deployment. +> +> For evaluation mode, set `isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `true`. In a production tenant, preserve the `includeTargets` from your existing SMS or voice policy rather than replacing them with the values shown in the example. Use a test tenant if you want to validate CYOT with different target users or groups. + +For SMS: + +```json +{ + "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.smsAuthenticationMethodConfiguration", + "state": "enabled", + "includeTargets": [ + { + "targetType": "group", + "id": "all_users", + "isRegistrationRequired": false, + "isUsableForSignIn": false + } + ], + "telecomProviderSettings": { + "url": "", + "appId": "", + "isEvaluationModeEnabled": false, + "migrationPercentage": 100 + } +} +``` + +For Voice: + +```json +{ + "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.voiceAuthenticationMethodConfiguration", + "state": "enabled", + "includeTargets": [ + { + "targetType": "group", + "id": "all_users", + "isRegistrationRequired": false, + "verificationMode": "voiceOneTimePasscode" + } + ], + "telecomProviderSettings": { + "url": "", + "appId": "", + "isEvaluationModeEnabled": false, + "migrationPercentage": 100 + } +} +``` + +### Move to production mode + +After evaluation succeeds: + +1. Set `telecomProviderSettings.isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `false`. +1. Set `telecomProviderSettings.migrationPercentage` to your initial traffic percentage. +1. Keep the existing production `includeTargets` unchanged. +1. Submit the policy update. +1. Read the configuration again and verify the endpoint URL, application client ID, evaluation mode, migration percentage, and targets. +1. Test [telecom provider delivery](#test-telecom-provider-delivery) before increasing traffic. + +### Increase traffic gradually + +1. Keep `isEvaluationModeEnabled` set to `false`. +1. Increase `migrationPercentage` in increments until you reach `100`. +1. Keep the endpoint URL, application client ID, and existing `includeTargets` unchanged while changing the migration percentage. +1. [Validate authentication and telecom provider delivery](#check-each-rollout-stage) after each change. +1. Increase the percentage after each stage validates successfully. To investigate an issue, hold at the current percentage and see [Monitor and troubleshoot](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> When each stage validates successfully, continue to 100 percent without delay. Completing your rollout early helps ensure uninterrupted authentication for your users. For dates, see [Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication](concept-sms-voice-retirement.md). + +## Step 5: Test the integration + +Use a test user with a phone number registered for SMS or voice. + + + +### Test in Evaluation + +1. In an InPrivate browser session, sign in as the test user and complete an SMS or voice authentication. +1. In the Azure portal, go to your **Function App** > **SendOtp** > **Invocations** and open the latest transaction. In **Invocation details**, confirm **Evaluation request completed** with HTTP `200`. +1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Monitoring & health** > **Audit logs** and filter by **Service: Azure MFA**. Open the latest entry and confirm **DeliveryMethod** is `CyotEvaluation`. + + + + +### Test provider delivery + +After evaluation succeeds, set `isEvaluationModeEnabled` to `false` and configure your initial `migrationPercentage`. + +1. In a new InPrivate browser session, sign in as the test user. Confirm the SMS or voice code arrives and authentication completes. +1. In the Azure portal, go to your **Function App** > **Invocations** and open the latest transaction. In **Invocation details**, confirm the request completed with HTTP `200`. +1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Audit logs** and filter by **Service: Azure MFA**. Open the latest entry and confirm **Delivery Method** is `Cyot`. +1. In your provider's portal, confirm the message was delivered. + +At a partial percentage, only some requests route through your provider, so make a few attempts. If something doesn't look right, see [Monitor and troubleshoot your own telephony provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). + +## Troubleshooting + +To diagnose integration issues, use the troubleshooting guide to identify whether the issue is with the Microsoft Entra configuration, Azure Function, telecom provider, or authentication flow. + +See [Monitor and troubleshoot your own telephony provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider) for diagnostic steps, logs, common issues, and remediation guidance. + +## Related content + +- [Monitor and troubleshoot](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). +- [Prevent telephony fraud when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md). +- [Plan for resiliency when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md).

modifiedFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/concept-phone-providers.md b/docs/identity/authentication/concept-phone-providers.md index b549c3cb3a3..2e6459825f8 100644 --- a/docs/identity/authentication/concept-phone-providers.md +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/concept-phone-providers.md @@ -1,51 +1,122 @@ --- -title: Choose a telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication -description: Learn about Choose Your Own Telephony Provider for SMS and voice authentication in Microsoft Entra ID. +title: Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication +description: Learn how CYOT works, available telecom providers, and how to plan setup, fraud protection, resiliency, and costs. ms.topic: concept-article -ms.date: 09/23/2026 -ai-usage: ai-generated +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted # Customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to understand Choose Your Own Telephony Provider so that I can plan continued use of SMS or voice authentication. --- -# Choose a telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication +# Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication -Microsoft Entra ID will support Choose Your Own Telephony Provider, which lets organizations continue using SMS or voice authentication with a supported telephony provider. You select a telephony provider through the Microsoft Security Store and manage the provider relationship for your organization. + -Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as [passkeys](concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md), instead of SMS or voice. Use a telephony provider only for user populations that have a business, regulatory, or technical requirement for telephony-based authentication. +Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) lets your organization use a supported telecom provider to deliver SMS and voice authentication for Microsoft Entra ID. + +With CYOT, Microsoft Entra continues to manage the authentication experience, including one-time passcode (OTP) generation and validation, while SMS messages and voice calls are delivered through the telecom provider that your organization selects and configures. + +CYOT gives your organization more control over telecom provider selection, geographic coverage, pricing, and telecom delivery. > [!IMPORTANT] -> Choose Your Own Telephony Provider isn't available to configure yet. Information about the providers participating in the private preview is available now. The configuration experience becomes available beginning October 30, 2026. +> Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as [passkeys](concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md), instead of SMS or voice. Use a telephony provider only for user populations that have a business, regulatory, or technical requirement for telephony-based authentication. + + + +## How CYOT works + +When SMS or voice authentication is required: + +1. Microsoft Entra initiates the authentication request. +1. Microsoft Entra sends the request to the CYOT integration deployed in your Azure subscription. +1. The integration sends the request to your configured telecom provider. +1. Your telecom provider delivers the SMS message or voice call to the user. +1. Microsoft Entra completes the authentication flow. + +The Azure Function deployed in your subscription connects Microsoft Entra with your telecom provider. + +:::image type="content" source="media/concept-phone-providers/telephony-provider-integration-diagram.jpeg" alt-text="Simplified CYOT architecture diagram showing Microsoft Entra connected to a telecom provider through an Azure Function in your Azure subscription." lightbox="media/concept-phone-providers/telephony-provider-integration-diagram.jpeg"::: ## Available telephony providers -Soprano and Telesign are the initial telephony providers available during the private preview. More providers will become available by general availability. +Select a supported telecom provider based on your organization's coverage, pricing, and other requirements. Review pricing and other commercial details for the available provider offers: -- Soprano: [Per-user offer](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/solutions/sopranodesignlimited1620113206416.soprano_entraid_per_user) or [per-transaction offer](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/solutions/sopranodesignlimited1620113206416.soprano_entraid_per_transaction) in Microsoft Security Store. -- Telesign: [Telesign Verify for Microsoft Entra](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/solutions/telesigncorporation1779799505747.telesign-verify-cyot-azure) in Microsoft Security Store. +- Soprano: [Per-user offer](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/solutions/sopranodesignlimited1620113206416.soprano_entraid_per_user) or [per-transaction offer](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/solutions/sopranodesignlimited1620113206416.soprano_entraid_per_transaction) in [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/). +- Telesign: [Telesign Verify for Microsoft Entra](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/solutions/telesigncorporation1779799505747.telesign-verify-cyot-azure) in [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/). +- Infobip. + +> [!NOTE] +> Provider availability, coverage, pricing, and commercial terms can vary. Review the provider's [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/) listing for the latest information before purchasing. + +## Understand your responsibilities + +With CYOT, your organization owns the Azure resources deployed in your subscription and your telecom provider account, so you keep full control over how they run. The guided deployment sets up the integration for you, and your team manages the Azure Function and provider account from there. + +| Owner | Responsibilities | +|---|---| +| Microsoft | Microsoft Entra authentication and the handoff to your endpoint. | +| Customer | Deploying and operating the integration, managing the telecom provider account, and configuring fraud controls. | +| Telephony provider | SMS and voice delivery, and offering fraud controls. | + +## Get started with CYOT + +At a high level, setting up CYOT involves: + +1. **Subscribe to a telecom provider.** Review the available provider offers in [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/) and purchase the offer that meets your organization's requirements. +1. **Set up the provider integration.** Deploy the integration in your Azure subscription and connect it to your provider. +1. **Create an SMS or voice profile.** Route SMS or voice authentication through your provider. +1. **Evaluate.** Validate the integration while Microsoft continues to deliver messages, so users aren't affected. +1. **Roll out.** Move traffic to your provider gradually, validating at each stage. + +For detailed instructions, see [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md). + + + +## Plan your deployment + +Before moving production authentication traffic to CYOT, consider fraud protection, resiliency, and costs based on your organization's requirements. + +### Prevent telephony fraud + +Work with your telecom provider to configure the fraud protection, destination, usage, and spending controls appropriate for your organization's traffic and risk requirements. + +See [Prevent telephony fraud when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md). + +### Plan for resiliency + +Plan the availability and recovery of the Azure resources and telecom provider used by your CYOT integration. + +Organizations with additional availability requirements can implement cross-region resiliency and, where appropriate, configure provider redundancy. + +See [Plan for resiliency when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md). + +### Understand costs + +CYOT can involve two separate categories of costs: -## How Choose Your Own Telephony Provider works +- Telecom provider costs for SMS and voice delivery through your selected provider. +- Azure costs for the Azure Function and supporting resources deployed in your subscription. -Your selected telephony provider delivers the SMS messages or voice calls that users need to complete authentication. Microsoft Entra ID continues to enforce your authentication method policies and coordinates the authentication experience. +Review both before moving production authentication traffic to CYOT. -Your organization is responsible for selecting a telephony provider, reviewing its regional coverage and terms, completing the provider agreement, configuring the provider for Microsoft Entra ID, and monitoring the service. +See [Estimate telecom-provider and Azure hosting costs](phone-providers-faq.yml#how-much-does-choose-your-own-telephony-provider-cost). -For the full transition schedule, see [Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication](concept-sms-voice-retirement.md). +## Troubleshoot CYOT -## Plan your Choose Your Own Telephony Provider deployment +To diagnose SMS or voice issues, identify whether the issue is in Microsoft Entra authentication and configuration, your CYOT integration, or telecom provider delivery. -Before you select a provider: +See [Troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider) for diagnostic guidance and information about where to get support. -- Identify the users who have a documented requirement for SMS or voice authentication. -- Confirm that a phishing-resistant method doesn't meet the requirement. -- Compare supported telephony providers based on geographic coverage, supported delivery channels, pricing, support, security, and compliance capabilities. -- Review procurement, privacy, and regulatory requirements with the appropriate teams in your organization. + -## Next steps +## Related content -- [Review frequently asked questions about telephony providers](phone-providers-faq.yml). -- [Prepare for the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication](concept-sms-voice-retirement.md). -- [Plan a passkey deployment](how-to-deploy-phishing-resistant-passwordless-authentication.md). -- [Review voice call authentication](concept-authentication-phone-options.md). +- [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md). +- [Prevent telephony fraud when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md). +- [Plan for resiliency when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md). +- [Troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md#monitor-and-troubleshoot-your-own-telephony-provider). +- [Estimate telecom-provider and Azure hosting costs](phone-providers-faq.yml#how-much-does-choose-your-own-telephony-provider-cost). +- [Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication](concept-sms-voice-retirement.md). +- [SMS-based authentication for Microsoft Entra ID](howto-authentication-sms-signin.md).

modifiedFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/identity/authentication/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md b/docs/identity/authentication/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md index 321fc2d826e..0c980c920ee 100644 --- a/docs/identity/authentication/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md +++ b/docs/identity/authentication/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md @@ -1,95 +1,164 @@ --- -title: Troubleshoot MFA voice call and SMS problems -description: Learn how to troubleshoot voice call and SMS problems with MFA, understand telecom delivery, and help Microsoft Support investigate delivery issues. +title: Troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider +description: Trace CYOT SMS and voice requests with audit logs, sign-in logs, and Function App logs to identify issues and contact the right support team. ms.topic: how-to -ms.date: 04/09/2026 +ms.date: 10/30/2026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1012 ms.reviewer: xueca -# Customer intent: As an authentication administrator, I want to troubleshoot voice call and SMS problems with multifactor authentication (MFA) for Microsoft Entra ID. +# Customer intent: As an authentication administrator, I want to identify and resolve CYOT authentication, integration, and telecom delivery issues. --- -# Troubleshoot MFA voice call and SMS problems -This article explains how to investigate and resolve problems with voice call or SMS sign-in methods for multifactor authentication (MFA). It explains how telecom delivery works behind the scenes, what Microsoft can and can't see, and what to expect during an investigation. +# Troubleshoot SMS and voice with your own telecom provider -## Move to modern, phishing-resistant authentication + + + -> [!IMPORTANT] -> Microsoft is committed to helping organizations adopt modern, phishing-resistant authentication methods. While telecom-based MFA provides an important layer of security, methods like passkeys, certificate-based authentication, and Windows Hello for Business offer stronger protection against interception and social engineering attacks. -> -> These methods also avoid the delivery variability inherent in global telecom networks. Microsoft recommends transitioning to these more secure alternatives: -> -> - [Passkeys (FIDO2)](concept-authentication-passwordless.md#fido2-security-keys) -> - [Windows Hello for Business](/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/) -> - [Certificate-based authentication](concept-certificate-based-authentication.md) +Use this article to trace SMS and voice requests end to end with Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT), find where a request stopped, and contact the right team to resolve it: Microsoft support, your Azure team, or your telecom provider. -## How global telecom delivery works + + + + -Microsoft works with primary telecom providers that have global reach. These providers rely on their own networks of suppliers, who control the routes for SMS and voice calls through local end-carrier networks. This supply chain represents thousands of individual carriers and routes around the globe. +## How a CYOT request flows -Microsoft maintains robust processes to help ensure successful delivery of every SMS and voice MFA request. However, once a request leaves the Microsoft network, delivery is delegated to external telecom providers. +Each request passes through four stages, and each stage is recorded in its own logs: -These providers often share the same end routes and carriers in a given destination country but might operate under different contractual agreements or traffic priorities. As a result, routing a request through a different provider doesn't always resolve the issue — the new request might follow the same downstream path and encounter the same obstacle. +| Stage | What happens | Where to look | +|---|---|---| +| 1. Microsoft Entra sends the request | Microsoft Entra requires an SMS or voice code and sends the request to your endpoint. | Microsoft Entra audit logs | +| 2. Your endpoint processes it | Your Function App receives the request and sends it to your telecom provider. | Function App logs | +| 3. Your provider delivers it | Your provider sends the SMS message or voice call to the user's phone. | Your provider's portal | +| 4. The user signs in | The user enters the code, and Microsoft Entra completes authentication. | Microsoft Entra sign-in logs | -## The journey of an SMS or voice MFA request +## Find the request in audit logs -When you sign in and an SMS or voice MFA challenge is triggered, Microsoft can confirm the following steps given a Correlation ID and timestamp: +1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a Reports Reader. +1. Go to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Audit logs**, and select the **Directory** tab. +1. Set the **Date range**, and add these filters: **Service: Azure MFA** and **Category: Authentication**. +1. Leave **Activity** set to **All** so you see both successful and failed requests. -1. **Request received.** Microsoft Entra generates the MFA request and constructs the payload for the SMS or voice request with the expected Microsoft or company branding. -1. **Provider selected.** Microsoft sends the request to one of multiple external third-party telecom providers matching your country code. -1. **Channel matched.** The request is routed through the correct channel (SMS or voice) per your configuration, selection, and policy requirements. -1. **Delivery confirmed.** The provider confirms receipt of the telecom request and marks it as successfully delivered with no alterations. +:::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-logs.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Audit logs filtered by Service Azure MFA and Category Authentication, showing CyotDeliverySucceeded and CyotDeliveryFailed activities." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-logs.png"::: -After the provider confirms delivery, the request enters external telecom networks where Microsoft doesn't have direct visibility. Problems that occur beyond this point require collaboration with the provider to investigate. +Select the request to open **Audit Log Details**, and note these values: -## What can go wrong after delivery to the provider +| Field | What it tells you | +|---|---| +| Activity Type | `CyotDeliverySucceeded` means your endpoint accepted the request. `CyotDeliveryFailed` means it didn't complete. | +| DeliveryMethod | `Cyot` for a live request through your provider. `CyotEvaluation` for an evaluation request. | +| Channel | `Sms` or `Voice`. | +| AuthenticationMethod | The method used, such as `OneWaySms` or `OneWayVoiceMobileOtp`. | +| Correlation ID | The identifier to share with support. | +| FailureReason | Why a failed request didn't complete. | -After the request reaches an external telecom provider, two types of problems can occur. +:::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-log-details.png" alt-text="Screenshot of Audit Log Details for CyotDeliverySucceeded with DeliveryMethod Cyot and Channel Voice." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/audit-log-details.png"::: -### The call or message is dropped or blocked + -The provider should confirm this issue to Microsoft. Common causes include: +## Check sign-in logs -- **Device-level configuration.** Even when all steps to send the message are correct, the device itself could refuse the call or route it to voicemail. Microsoft automatically retries these failures across different providers. -- **Carrier-level blocking.** The carrier might block the call or message due to international automated fraud detection systems. -- **Regional availability issues.** In rare cases, the message is dropped due to availability issues in a specific country. Microsoft and its providers have robust retry and reroute mechanisms for these scenarios and post automated outage communications when the impact is broadly reported. +Use sign-in logs to confirm whether the user completed authentication. -### The call or message is altered by a downstream carrier +1. Go to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**. +1. Find the sign-in by user and time, and open it. +1. On **Authentication Details**, review the method, whether the step succeeded, and the result detail. -Because the provider already confirmed delivery, Microsoft can only see a successful delivery per its specification. When message content is altered: +Sign-in logs show the method as **Text message** or **Voice**. To confirm that the request was sent through your provider, use audit logs. -- The customer should provide evidence that the message received on their device didn't appear with the expected branding or channel. -- Microsoft collaborates with the provider to understand the end-carrier behavior taken on behalf of the request. -- The provider will likely correct the route for the affected country code or phone number to avoid carriers that aren't honoring the original message contract. + + -## What to expect during an investigation +## Check Function App logs -Due to the complexity of global telecom routing and limited visibility beyond the provider, telecom delivery investigations involve coordination across multiple companies and stakeholders. +Use your Function App logs to see how your endpoint processed the request and what it returned to Microsoft Entra. -### Timeline +1. In the Azure portal, open the Function App created by setup. +1. Go to **Monitoring** > **Application Insights**, and open the linked Application Insights resource. +1. Select **Logs**, and run the following query for the time of the attempt: -Investigations into downstream customer-reported delivery issues can take 4–6 weeks. The provider checks their logs and, if no issue is found locally, queries downstream partners who might use additional providers. + ```kusto + AppRequests + | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) + | where Url has "/api/SendOtp" + | project TimeGenerated, ResultCode, Success, DurationMs, OperationId + | order by TimeGenerated desc + ``` -### Root cause analysis (RCA) policy +`ResultCode` shows what your Function App returned to Microsoft Entra. To see your provider's response for the same request, query `AppTraces` with its `OperationId`. -Microsoft doesn't publish RCAs for issues that originate with external telecom providers. Carriers often don't share root cause details with Microsoft due to international visibility and competitive agreements. + + + + + + + + + + + + + -## Help with the investigation +## Identify who can help -To help Microsoft Support investigate provider-related issues: +Use what you see in audit logs to find the right contact. -- **Submit a Correlation ID and timestamp** for the sign-ins that need investigation. You can find these values in the [sign-in logs](~/identity/monitoring-health/concept-sign-ins.md). The Correlation ID returns all Request IDs associated with the sign-in. +| What you see | What to check | Contact | +|---|---|---| +| No CYOT activity in audit logs | Confirm the date range and filters, that the user is included in SMS or voice targeting, and that a new phone challenge was required. | Microsoft support | +| Only `CyotEvaluation` activity | The profile is in **Evaluation**. Switch to **Production** to route traffic through your provider. | No support needed | +| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `EndpointClientError` | Your endpoint rejected the request. Check your Function App logs and authentication settings. | Your Azure team | +| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `EndpointServerError` | Your endpoint returned an error or didn't respond in time. Check your Function App logs and your provider's status. | Your Azure team | +| `CyotDeliveryFailed` with `NonceMismatch` | Your endpoint's response didn't match what Microsoft Entra expects. Compare any customizations with the CYOT sample. | Your Azure team | +| `CyotDeliverySucceeded`, but the user didn't receive the code | Your endpoint accepted the request. Check your provider's delivery records. | Your telecom provider | +| The user received the code, but sign-in failed | Check the sign-in logs for an expired, reused, or incorrect code. | Microsoft support | +| Delivery blocked to certain countries/regions, fraud blocks, or unexpected charges | Review your provider's fraud, destination, and spending controls. | Your telecom provider | - To view the sign-in logs from the Microsoft Entra admin center: +> [!TIP] +> When a request times out, check your provider's records before you try again. Your provider might have already accepted the original request. - 1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Reports Reader](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader). - 1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**. + + - :::image type="content" source="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/sign-in-log-correlation-id.png" alt-text="Screenshot that shows the Date and Correlation ID fields in the sign-in logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center." lightbox="media/troubleshoot-voice-call-sms/sign-in-log-correlation-id.png"::: +## Contact support -- **Provide fresh samples.** End carriers often require Correlation IDs from the last 48–72 hours. Older requests may not propagate to the final end carrier in time for investigation. You may be asked to provide multiple samples. -- **Provide evidence of altered messages.** If the message you received didn't appear with the expected branding or channel, share a screenshot or description of what you received. +| Contact | Covers | How to reach | +|---|---|---| +| Microsoft support | Authentication method policy, Microsoft Entra authentication, and the request to your endpoint | [Get support for Microsoft Entra](/entra/fundamentals/how-to-get-support) | +| Your Azure team | Your Function App, its configuration, and Azure resources | Internal. For Azure platform issues, contact Azure support. | +| Your telecom provider | Provider account, delivery, fraud controls, and usage charges | Support details in the provider's [Microsoft Security Store](https://securitystore.microsoft.com/) listing | + + + + + + + + +### Information to include + +- Tenant ID, channel (SMS or voice), and the UTC time of the attempt. +- The audit log **Correlation ID**, `DeliveryMethod`, and `FailureReason`. +- Your provider's transaction ID, if available. +- Any recent configuration changes. + + + ## Related content -- [Voice call authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID](concept-authentication-phone-options.md) -- [Configure and enable users for SMS-based authentication using Microsoft Entra ID](howto-authentication-sms-signin.md) \ No newline at end of file +- [Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider by using APIs](how-to-set-up-sms-voice-api.md). +- [Plan for resiliency and high availability with your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-reliability.md). +- [Prevent telephony fraud when using your own telecom provider](choose-your-own-telephony-fraud-costs.md). +- [Audit logs in Microsoft Entra ID](/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-audit-logs). +- [Monitor Microsoft Entra sign-ins](/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-sign-ins). +- [CYOT sign-in monitoring][sample-sign-in-monitoring]. +- [CYOT setup troubleshooting][sample-troubleshooting]. +- [Integrate Microsoft Entra logs with Azure Monitor](/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-integrate-activity-logs-with-azure-monitor-logs). +- [Analyze Microsoft Entra activity logs with Log Analytics](/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-analyze-activity-logs-log-analytics). + +[sample-sign-in-monitoring]: https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/epp-packages-193-1/docs/SIGN-IN-MONITORING.md +[sample-troubleshooting]: https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/blob/epp-packages-193-1/setup/docs/Troubleshooting.md

groups.summary: A new article explains how to configure telecom-provider fraud, destination, channel, spending, and alert controls; secure the CYOT integration; monitor activity; and respond to suspected fraud. The documentation explains CYOT delivery dependencies and resiliency approaches, including multi-region Azure Front Door deployments, secondary telecom providers, failover testing, capacity planning, and associated costs. The new guide explains how to connect Microsoft Entra SMS and voice authentication to a telecom provider using CYOT, including purchasing, Azure deployment, permissions, policy configuration, testing, and rollout. The article now explains CYOT architecture, Azure Function integratio

groups.title: external-id
groups.summary: The custom policies guidance now includes a screenshot of the Migration Policy Analyzer UI and updated author metadata.

groups.title: id-governance
groups.summary: The documentation no longer includes the note that nested group drift is excluded and that reports compare assignments with users directly assigned to a group. The Agent ID default inactivity policy page updates links to related lifecycle policy and end-user agent management documentation.

groups.title: global-secure-access
groups.summary: The configuration guide no longer includes the note that a special Entra Admin Center link might be needed during the September 2026 rollout to view custom header details in Global Secure Access traffic logs.
